merger_description:
ANZLAFF Sub 2, through its trustee The Trust Company Limited, (the **Purchaser**) proposes to acquire the remaining 50% of shares in Benditi Pastoral Co Pty Ltd (**Benditi Pastoral**) from Benditi Holding Co Pty Ltd, as trustee for the Benditi Holding Co Trust (the **Vendor**), pursuant to a Call and Put Option deed dated 4 December 2025 (the **Deed**) (the **Acquisition**).

The Vendor granted the Purchaser a Call Option under the Deed to acquire all of the remaining shares it holds in Benditi Pastoral. The parties entered into the Deed simultaneous to ANZLAFF Sub 2 acquiring an initial 50% of the shares in Benditi Pastoral. The Purchaser intends to exercise the Call Option on, or abouts, 17 July 2026.

ANZLAFF Sub 2 is a sub-trust of New Forests Australia New Zealand Landscapes and Forestry Fund (**ANZLAFF**), which invests in a diversified portfolio of forestry and agricultural land assets and associated processing assets. Both trusts are administered by professional trustee companies, The Trust Company Limited and The Trust Company (Australia) Limited respectively (subsidiaries of Perpetual Limited).

ANZLAFF and ANZLAFF Sub 2 are managed by New Forests Asset Management Pty Limited (**NF Management**). NF Management is a wholly owned subsidiary of New Forests Pty Limited, which is a global investment manager focused on nature-based real assets and natural capital strategies.

Benditi Pastoral operates a beef cattle grazing enterprise near Yarrowitch and Walcha, in the New England region of NSW. This involves the breeding, growing and finishing of beef cattle, as well as the management of the cattle herd and associated land and infrastructure.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition. In particular, there is very small horizontal overlap
between ANZLAFF Sub 2 (and its connected entities) and Benditi
Pastoral in the production of cattle in Australia, and the increase in
its share of supply arising from the Acquisition would be small.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
